messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int fact(int n) { if (n <= 1) return 1; return n * fact(n); }

Question: What is fact(3)?
The student answered: it never stops

The student understands this correctly: The argument has to change toward the base case; calling with the same or a growing value never reaches it.

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: sure of themselves, plain English, one sentence of 8 to 18 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["The function calls itself with the same n every time, so it never moves toward the ending condition.", "Since n stays exactly 3 in the recursive call, there is no path that reaches the return 1 line.", "That return statement keeps calling fact(n) with n unchanged, so nothing ever brings it closer to the base case.", "The argument inside the return never shrinks or changes, so the stopping point at n <= 1 is never reached.", "Calling fact(n) again with the very same value means the same call happens over and over forever."]}

sentences: The function calls itself with the same n every time, so it never moves toward the ending condition.
Since n stays exactly 3 in the recursive call, there is no path that reaches the return 1 line.
That return statement keeps calling fact(n) with n unchanged, so nothing ever brings it closer to the base case.
The argument inside the return never shrinks or changes, so the stopping point at n <= 1 is never reached.
Calling fact(n) again with the very same value means the same call happens over and over forever.
